audit_verdicts_index.claim: Moving-range (MRbar/d2) estimated-parameter ARL0 degradation for the module's Shewhart Individuals chart (L=3). The Individuals-chart textbook-default sigma estimator is the average moving range, sigma_hat=MRbar/d2, NOT the sample S used by the prior receipt. An exact closed-form MR sampling variance (adjacent moving-range correlation rho=-1/2) -- validated against pinned-seed correlated Monte Carlo -- yields a Patnaik effective df nu_eff(m) BELOW the S/c4 df (m-1), and the estimated-parameter guaranteed (5th-pct) in-control ARL0 for MR/d2 sits BELOW the S/c4 value at every finite baseline m. This quantifies the 'MR/d2 degrades at least as much (conservative direction)' assertion that estparam-arl-degradation-v1 left unquantified.

audit_verdicts_index.claim: Estimated-parameter (Phase-II) run-length degradation of the EWMA(0.20,3) and two-sided CUSUM(0.5,5) arms of the live three-detector union, via the exact conditional reduction Y ~ N(-U/W, 1/W^2) (Jones-Champ-Rigdon 2001/2004) with Brook-Evans Markov-chain ARL solvers generalized to non-unit variance. The memory detectors degrade MORE than Shewhart: at a 30-observation baseline the guaranteed (5th-pct) ARL0 retains only 9.5% (EWMA) and 9.8% (CUSUM) of its known-parameter value versus 13.3% for Shewhart, and the guaranteed (95th-pct) union false-alarm count over the module's 30-batch KPI window rises from the known-parameter 0.199 to 1.73991 -- outside the locked budget of 1.5.
does_not_close: Does NOT establish real-batch acceptability, product qualification, EHS acceptability, or batch-release authority.
Assumes i.i.d. normal in-control data; autocorrelation and non-normality are not modeled and remain open.

Uses sigma_hat = S/c4; the MRbar/d2 estimator actually defaulted to by Individuals charts is strictly worse (ARE 0.605), so the memory-arm guaranteed ARL0 reported here is an upper bound, not the operating value. The MRbar/d2 x EWMA/CUSUM cross is still open.
The two-sided CUSUM ARL uses the Lucas-Crosier 1/ARL = 1/ARL+ + 1/ARL- combination, which is an approximation (validated to <=6% against Montgomery Table 9.4, not exact).

The union false-alarm figure is a Bonferroni rate bound summing per-chart 30/ARL0; it does not model the strong positive dependence among the three charts (they read the same stream), so it is conservative by construction.
No prospective time-ordered 30-batch pilot is checked in; this is a theory characterization, not a false-alarm measurement on real batches.
Out-of-control (ARL1) performance under estimated parameters, and the recall >=90% half of the KPI, are not characterized here.

honest_headline: Known-parameter (infinite-baseline) reference: Shewhart ARL0=370.4, EWMA(0.2,3) ARL0=559.804, union false-alarm rate 0.1985 per 30 batches -- all four Markov-chain/geometric solvers reproduce published anchors (Montgomery 2020 Table 9.4; Siegmund 1985; Shewhart 1931) to <=3.1% relative error. At the module's actual m=20-25 pilot baseline size (per docs/mission.md), guaranteed (5th-percentile) in-control run length collapses to roughly 9.5-13.3% of the known-parameter value at m=30 across all three detector arms (retention {'cusum': 0.0983, 'ewma': 0.0952, 'shewhart': 0.1329}), and the locked <=1.5-expected-false-alarm/30-batch union budget is NOT met at m=30 (observed 1.73991 at p95, under the S/c4 estimator). The smallest tabulated baseline meeting that budget is m=50, roughly double the module's current pilot baseline size -- this is a decision-relevant gap for any prospective 30-batch pilot design, not a pass/fail on module correctness. That m=50 finding was computed under sigma_hat=S/c4, which the source receipt itself flags as an upper bound (the MRbar/d2 estimator the Individuals chart actually defaults to is strictly worse, ARE=0.605); the MRbar/d2 x EWMA/CUSUM cross that would close this gap is listed under `awaiting` below.
